traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements from docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are fully implemented: - Rule naming and aliasing are wired so that traceability/prefer-supports-annotation is the primary rule and traceability/prefer-implements-annotation is a deprecated alias (src/index.ts, docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md, migration guide). - The rule emits optional, configurable recommendations for legacy @story + @req patterns, is off by default, and can be set to warn or error via standard ESLint severity configuration. - Auto-fix safely transforms single-story @story + @req (including multiple @req lines) into a single @supports line while preserving JSDoc structure and non-traceability tags. - Multi-story and mixed legacy/@supports patterns are detected and reported but not auto-fixed, with clear messages. - When the rule is disabled, legacy @story/@req annotations remain fully valid and validation continues to be provided by the existing core rules. - Auto-fix output is constrained to cases that the parser can interpret unambiguously and is structured to pass @supports validation. - Comprehensive unit tests and documentation directly reference this story and its requirement IDs, and all related tests pass, confirming behavior and configuration semantics.
Given the current code, tests, and documentation, this story is completely implemented and verifiably passing.
